verdicts.reason: Quotes verified verbatim. 19.05.01-live-count-manifest-state.md:36 defines '| **Remaining** | Sellable right now (= capacity − killed − held − paid − comp) |' and `grep -rn carted 19.05-box-office-counts-drops/` returns ZERO hits — the counter does not exist anywhere in the sub-domain that authors the counter set. 19.01.02-capacity-manifest-allocations-holds.md:34 states the invariant 'licensed capacity = killed + held + comp + paid + carted + remaining', :43 lists `carted` as its own bucket, and :214 (D-06) enforces it 'at every mutation'. The two are arithmetically incompatible: 19.05.01's remaining is 19.01.02's remaining PLUS carted. This is not a scoping difference — 19.01.02:37 explicitly cedes ownership ('The counters themselves are owned and reported by 19.05.01') and 19.05.01:65 (D-09) claims it ('The counter set itself is authored **here**'), so the omission is authoritative, not an abbreviation. Searched for a reconciliation and found none: 19.05-box-office-counts-drops-cx.md has no `carted` mention (CX-01..CX-06 cover drops, pacing, walk-up, close); 19.02.04-queue-waiting-room-cart-hold.md:27/:43/:88 (D-04) specifies only that cart holds return to their 'source pool', never how `remaining` reports them; the single domain-CX hit (ticketing-box-office-cx.md:166) is about per-buyer limit counting, not the count's counter set. 19.05.01 Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 (:73-75) cover minimum disclosure, single-party certification and blended-source boundary — none touches carts; no [PENDING]/[OWNER] marker anywhere near either statement. The auditor's supporting point that 19.01.02 is itself split holds up: :122 ('Operator sees a lower available figure than `remaining` during on-sale, with carted quantity stated') and :154 ('Available-to-hold shown separately from `remaining` because `carted` is untouchable') are only coherent if carted sits INSIDE remaining, which D-06 forbids. Divergence is real and consequential: under the D-06 reading the storefront boolean goes false while carts are outstanding; under 19.05.01's formula it stays true, exposing oversell on the last units, and 19.05.01 D-01 (:57) forbids any consumer from computing its own count to compensate. Two normative statements that cannot both hold → blocking upheld as filed.

Quotes are accurate but the reconciliation the finding says is missing is four lines below the offending line, and the offending line points at it. 19.01.03-fee-structure-all-in-pricing.md:36 reads '+ amortised per-order mandatory fees        [see per-order handling below]' — the bracketed pointer is part of the formula, not decoration. :40, the paragraph it points to, resolves the mechanic explicitly: 'Per-order fees (a single handling charge, delivery) apply once per order, not per ticket. Mandatory per-order fees are disclosed in the headline where a jurisdiction requires all mandatory charges to be shown upfront; the buyer sees the per-order component itemised at cart before commit.' DT-05 (:92), which the finding quotes, states the same resolution in its own rejection text and the finding does not engage with it: 'Per-order fees are disclosed at order level in the headline math but remain a distinct order-scoped line for settlement and refund correctness.' D-05 (:116) forbids amortising 'into per-ticket lines' for 'settlement and refunds' — the exact scope :40 leaves order-level. So the three normative statements agree; only the single word 'amortised' in the code block is loose, and it is cross-referenced to its own correction. The claimed forced invention is also tracked, not silent: :40 states 'Which mandatory-fee and tax components must appear *in* the headline versus *disclosed alongside* it is jurisdiction-specific (Q-01)', and Q-01 (:126) is marked RESOLVED to the US profile with an explicit named residual routed onward — 'the *named* US instruments — which mandatory fees and taxes sit inside the headline, state fee caps, municipal amusement taxes — are the empirical legal work D-72 explicitly declines to assert here', Deferred To '/create-prd-security'. Two competent implementers reading D-05 + DT-05 + :40 converge on face + per-ticket fees in the tier headline with the per-order component disclosed at order level; neither invents a division denominator, because no text asks for one.

Quotes verified verbatim, but the finding reads an Edge Cases row as a supported feature. 19.11-rsvp-free-private-event-admission.md:48 sets the table's columns as 'Scenario | What Happens | User Sees' — so ':56 | Someone RSVPs for 6 | Free events attract inflated party sizes | Cap counts heads, not RSVPs (D-05) |' is a failure mode plus the rule that defeats it, not a party-booking path. Nothing in the file describes a party-size input, a guest-name field, or a multi-head record: the flow is one-tap-per-person three separate times — Role Lens Fan :21 ('RSVPs to a free show and turns up. One tap; no checkout, no card, no fee'), Happy Path step 3 :41 ('Shares the link with the client's team; **each person** RSVPs with one tap'), and Event Lifecycle Open :80 ('Fan sees a one-tap RSVP; no checkout'). D-05 and D-06 are the two halves of one rule, not a contradiction: :57 supplies the case D-05 exists for — 'Same Fan RSVPs twice (double-tap, two devices, re-opened link) | One human, one admission record — the second tap is idempotent, not a second head against the cap' — i.e. RSVP submissions and heads can differ by de-duplication, which is exactly what 'counts heads, not RSVPs' asserts, and exactly what D-06 (:117) and DT-03 (:93) mean by 'one head per person'. Under that reading D-02's scannable-record-per-admitted-body requirement (:113) is satisfied trivially: six people means six identity-keyed records. The finding's three invented questions collapse — a party of 6 is six RSVPs, the barcode is one-per-person so 19.04.01's use-once rule is untouched, and one-tap self-release returns the one seat that Fan holds. The comparison to 19.03.01 D-05 (:117, admission units and `+1` spend) is not a like-for-like gap: guest list has an explicit `+1` field in its submission model (19.03.01:29), and 19.11 has no analogous field to disambiguate. Two competent implementers converge on one-tap-one-head.

Verified against the files. ticketing-box-office-index.md:27-28 reads '**9 sub-domains, 3 domain-level features, 38 leaf features.** All `[SURFACE]` — breadth pass;\n> depth is allocated by MoSCoW at Step 5', and every Children row :32-43 carries `[SURFACE]`, including :43 for 19.12. Reality contradicts it on every row: reading line 5 of each child, 19.12-ticket-delivery-fan-wallet.md is '[DEEP]', 19.10 and 19.11 are '[PARTIAL]', eight of nine sub-domain indexes are '[BREADTH]' (19.08 alone still '[SURFACE]'), and 17 files across the domain carry a '[DEEP]' status line. No marker, no caveat — asserted as current fact in the pipeline key file every downstream workflow reads first, and it also compounds finding #005 by naming MoSCoW as the future allocator of depth after MoSCoW has run. (Minor overcount in the evidence: the finding says '32 [DEEP] markers'; 17 files carry a [DEEP] status line. Not load-bearing.) Warning as filed.

Every quote verifies, including the one that refutes the finding. 19.01.04-seating-model-ga-reserved-seat-maps.md:31 does assert 'Seat maps are a room asset (domain 16)...' — but the file does not leave that assertion standing silently. Q-01 at :94 quotes the offending sentence verbatim and negates it in the file's own Open Questions table: '**Collision recorded, not resolved**: the same DT-04 declines seat identities and map geometry — *"The room does **not** carry **seat identities or map geometry** ... Both domains are pointing at each other"* — so this file's assertion that *"seat maps are a room asset (domain 16)"* is wrong, and the reconciliation is tracked as `16.01.02` Q-02.' The row's Owner is 'Agent' and its Deferred-To column ends '· seat-map ownership collision → `16.01.02` Q-02' — an owner and a named target, which is a well-formed tracked deferral, not a silent contradiction. The finding's own words concede the tracking exists and object only that the target 'sits outside domain 19'; a cross-domain ownership collision is properly tracked in the domain that must decide it, and the same collision is independently visible from 19's side at 19.01.05:118 (Q-02 residual) and ticketing-box-office-index.md:110 (Q-12 point 1). Impact is further bounded: 19.01.04 Q-02 (:95) records MoSCoW placing reserved/mixed seating at 'could' — 'GA must, reserved could' — so the seat-map path is not v1 inventory at all. Refuted as tracked-deferral; the residual is unremediated prose adjacent to its own printed correction, not a forced invention.

Quotes verify at 19.04.04-door-age-id-verification.md:27 and :35 (Happy Path step 1), but the file supplies the correct rule itself, definitively, and the finding quotes the very row that does it. Q-04 at :115 reads '**RESOLVED — neither: 16 carries no audience age restriction at all.**', explains why (16.01.06 D-06's five locked statutory slots, and that domain 16's only `age` reference sits inside the hirer-requirements slot, 'what the venue demands of the **hirer** — not the audience restriction this feature consumes'), and then states the replacement behaviour in plain normative terms: '**There is therefore no upstream default to inherit, and the restriction is Operator-declared per show here.**' Nothing is left to invent — the sourcing rule is stated, the residual is scoped and routed ('adding a room-level default would reopen a locked owner decision (16.01.06 D-06, ratified as DQ-14.2) — an owner call, not a spec gap', Deferred To '`/create-prd`'), and the domain index corroborates at :110 (Q-12 point 3) with the same conclusion and the same onward route. An implementer who reads the file's Open Questions — the table this tree uses for exactly this purpose, and which carries three other live questions for this feature — cannot build the phantom inheritance. This is unremediated prose upstream of its own printed resolution, not a divergence: both competent implementers land on Operator-declared-per-show. Refuted as answered-elsewhere.
